candidates.text:
\boxed{\dfrac{27}{35}}

There are \(2^3-1=7\) non-empty subsets, each with prior probability \(1/7\).

The observed sequence is red, blue, red. Its likelihood is zero unless the subset contains **both** red and blue, so only two subsets survive:

- \(S=\{R,B\}\) (size 2): each draw is red or blue with probability \(1/2\), so
  \[
  P(\text{data}\mid S)=\left(\frac12\right)^3=\frac18.
  \]
- \(S=\{R,G,B\}\) (size 3): each color has probability \(1/3\), so
  \[
  P(\text{data}\mid S)=\left(\frac13\right)^3=\frac1{27}.
  \]

All other subsets have likelihood \(0\). By Bayes' rule,
\[
P(S=\{R,B\}\mid\text{data})
= \frac{\frac17\cdot\frac18}{\frac17\cdot\frac18+\frac17\cdot\frac1{27}}
= \frac{\frac18}{\frac18+\frac1{27}}
= \frac{27}{27+8}
= \frac{27}{35}.
\]
